title: Made a virtual DJ Booth and Nightclub using Godot, Claude, and Blender
author: DifferencePlastic378
selftext:
Hi!  
Just wanted to share my silly project. I enjoy writing lyrics and singing melodies Acapella then converting them with AI. I also have this idea of a "virtual nightclub" where in twitch chat or live youtube chat people could join the dance floor (Pick their dancer "shape, colors, and name"). They could then "dance" by controlling their avatar with basic commands via chat. 

This entire scene was made with in 2 days:    

* Claude Code Fable with Opus and Sonnet sub agents
* Godot 4.7
* Blender 5.3
* vRoid

So for all the models and shaders you see Claude code worked on it. The patterning on the records and other textures are largely Claude code including the jacket shader. 

A lot of my workflow focuses on "Research industry standards for X" or gathering reference images for my goals for Claude to understand the end state. 

I then describe any problems in detail I have. 

I initially pitched my concept to Claude and then walked through the feasibility with tools that existing paying careful attention to the licensing since I wanted to use this commercially to make a DJ scene while playing through my songs remixed for a hardcore gaming mix. 

I chose Godot over Unity because Godot has built in volumetric fog and the files on disk are very friendly with Claude. 

I realized that honestly it is hard to get consistency with "generative AI" so I'm trying to focus on "All math" workflows where possible because it is a lot easier to achieve what I want. 

A lot of the process is still built piece by piece just like you would if you were doing it by hand, just accelerated.

What do you guys think? Is this worthwhile?   
If you have questions about anything let me know!

I used to do product management and so I’m used to asking engineers for things 🤭
